soundness_flags.label: ass:covariance-consistency
soundness_flags.one_line: The condition is labeled a standard fixed-dimensional plug-in covariance result, but the cited Hsieh proposition proves consistency only of its scalar fixed-weight stacked variance estimator, not operator-norm consistency of this new full cross-fitted score covariance matrix.

soundness_flags.label: ass:covariance-consistency
soundness_flags.one_line: With fixed M, bounded clipped inverse weights, the fourth-moment bound, and the stated off-fold nuisance-rate realization, this covariance convergence should be derived for the displayed estimator rather than inserted as an additional load-bearing premise.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:joint-system-limit and thm:separate-joint-frontier / technical_internal_limitation
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Optimality is only within the fixed finite-dimensional constant linear span of retained pairwise DDD scores, not the semiparametric efficiency bound for the full conditional-moment DDD model.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The field claim is joint score-span GMM optimality, inference, and the separate-versus-joint frontier for fixed T, retained comparisons, and prespecified aggregate weights.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 27-29, Theorem 6.3, Proposition 6.4, Proposition 6.5, and equations (6.9)-(6.15)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 6.3 gives a fixed-weight stacked event-study CLT; Proposition 6.4 includes shared-control covariance; Proposition 6.5 proves consistency of the scalar stacked variance estimator, not operator-norm consistency of a full cross-fitted covariance matrix.

The paper derives efficient staggered-DiD/event-study influence functions using multiple comparison groups and periods and an attaining nonparametric estimator; its model has no DDD eligibility contrast.

The paper derives efficient influence functions for canonical panel and repeated-cross-section DDD designs and proposes nuisance-based estimation, but not staggered comparison-cohort overidentification.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 3.1, equations (3.4)-(3.8), especially p. C10 discussion of the crude o(N^-1/4) requirement
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines K-fold cross-fitting for orthogonal scores and describes o(N^-1/4) nuisance convergence as a crude sufficient condition in smooth problems.
The article establishes large-sample properties for estimators based on population orthogonality conditions, providing generic GMM rather than a DDD score construction.

The article characterizes semiparametric efficiency in models with nuisance functions and overidentified unconditional moments and shows optimally weighted two-step GMM can attain its efficiency bound.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 57(298), 1962, pp. 348-368
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article applies system-wide generalized least squares and reports asymptotic efficiency gains over equation-by-equation least squares when disturbances are correlated.
The article is the published triple-difference reference for the potential-outcomes DDD setup and identifying parallel-trends logic cited as supporting background.
